A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CASE-Bench and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G. The retained material can be matched across renumbering and substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-annotation experiments, statistical analyses of contextual effects, LLM evaluations, and appendix case studies and smaller-model results.

after.justification: v4 retains original human and LLM experiments and additionally reports DeepSeek-R1 and Llama-Guard-3-8B evaluations.

M1.justification: The core CASE-Bench method retains the same CI parameters, GPT-4o context generation followed by manual revision, and binary, direct-score, and normalized-token-probability judging approaches. The new classifier-specific input handling concerns comparator evaluation.

E1.justification: Both versions use 450 SORRY-Bench queries spanning 45 categories, with 900 final query-context pairs and the same five human-study conditions. The new model evaluations and replacement appendix case study use existing coverage; no additional dataset, domain, or population is evaluated.

E2.justification: v4 adds DeepSeek-R1 to Table 2 and evaluates the dedicated safety classifier Llama-Guard-3-8B in new Table 3. These extend comparison to reasoning and specialized moderation models. The original seven main-table models and five smaller models in Appendix G remain.

E3.justification: v4 specifies always-unsafe labels for child-related-crimes queries and excludes that category from the plotted K-W analysis, whereas v1 reports its varying contextual human judgments. The new Llama-Guard experiment introduces a user/agent conversation adapter and with/without-context testing. The principal metrics, annotation design, and general-purpose judging protocols remain.

E4.justification: v4 adds the Llama-Guard context-removal comparison. Appendix E.3.2 replaces the child-related-harms case study with social-stereotype promotion. The religion-promotion case study and the three-model CI-parameter ablation retain their analytical questions.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same power-analysis parameters, 21 annotations per task, z-tests, K-W tests, Bonferroni threshold, and averaging of three stochastic direct-score outputs. No new seed reporting, confidence intervals, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Main and appendix results are extensively updated: Claude-3.5's score accuracy changes from 90.9% to 90.1%, and Llama-3-8B's score-based unsafe recall changes from 69.6% to 96.6%. New results include DeepSeek-R1's 88.6% score accuracy and Llama-Guard's 54.1%/60.1% accuracy without/with context. Reported non-significant categories decrease from four to three following exclusion of child-related crimes. Changed labeling prevents interpreting the cross-version score updates as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The CI framework and equations for normalized safe-token probability and binary cross-entropy are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v4 introduces no substantive mathematical derivation or formal assumption change.

C1.justification: v4 explicitly frames the benchmark's contribution around LLM safety-judgment ability and adds a contribution concerning framework applications and future directions. The central claims about contextual effects, CI-based representation, human safety ratings, and over-refusal remain.

C2.justification: Beyond the retained Appendix A limitations, new Section 6 develops concrete context-verification and prompt-attack mitigation mechanisms. v4 also interprets DeepSeek-R1's performance as suggesting benefits from reasoning and attributes Llama-Guard's limitations to scale and contextual training. It adds an explicit child-safety boundary and misuse discussion, while removing Appendix B's explanation of ambiguous human judgments.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds the Llama-Guard conversation template, accompanied by token-probability extraction details in Section 5.2.2. Existing prompts and the two-A100, 3–6-hour computing statement remain. The standalone reproducibility section and API-versioning caveat disappear, although both abstracts already provide the public code/data link.

R1.justification: v4 adds contextual-toxicity motivation through Zhou et al., DeepSeek-R1 references, and literature on prompt-injection defenses, instruction hierarchy, and prompt tuning. It also softens the first-to-apply-power-analysis assertion. The principal positioning against safety and over-refusal benchmarks remains.

P1.justification: v4 edits the title, contribution list, CI descriptions, and related-work prose. It inserts a Discussion section, recasts Ethics as an Impact Statement, and removes the standalone Reproducibility section. Most of the original argument sequence and appendix prose are retained.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, with widespread resizing and relocation. The CI ablation changes from horizontal bars in side-by-side panels to vertical bars in stacked panels. v4 removes v1 Figure 3's human-response overview, adds the classifier table, and replaces the appendix's child-related case-study figure.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves practical relevance through the reasoning-model and dedicated-classifier evaluations, documented classifier adapter, and more concrete discussion of trusted context. The core empirical foundation was already present in v1. Removing the category-wide human-response plot and child-related case study reduces diagnostic detail, limiting the net improvement.
